findings.reason: the section must either state a second slice for the pre-collapse form (keeping card interiors) or drop that recognised form, because as written the byte-identity test the node iterates against cannot hold for the pre-collapse form.
findings.text: §16 states all three recognised fingerprint forms are produced from "the same sliced prose", but the pre-collapse (legacy) form keeps landed-card interiors whereas the slicer subtracts "every landed card's interior except its heading element", and `_AuthoredProseParser` drops card interiors only when `skip_landed_cards=True` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:213,230,242`), the `legacy=False` path keeping them whole (line 430 calls `_authored_prose(document)`); so one slicer cannot reproduce both the present whole-document form and the pre-collapse form, and §16 names no producer for the latter

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — `section_prose` on `reckon/_plan_html.py` is proposed as the single producer of the prose behind all three fingerprint forms, but it cannot produce the pre-collapse form whose prose keeps landed-card interiors, so the design leaves an unnamed second producer.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the plan extends owners rather than forking: `structured_section_spans` gains `every_marked_element` on `reckon/_plan_html.py`, `_TAG_RE` and `section_record_id` are reused as-is, `roadmap.implementable_sections` is read unchanged, and `recovery._plan_review_pending` is superseded rather than sat beside (the done-when requires `grep -n 'read_plan_review(' reckon/crew/recovery.py` to return nothing).
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1480, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23. §16 adds exactly one public definition (`section_prose`, 1480→1481) and its own accounting names the reader merge that funds it, states the retired `legacy` parameter and the moved private names, and records that the refusal reuses the `plan-review-missing` family (refusal_families +0); §20 adds none and retires none. The supplied count 1480 matches the section's stated base.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §16 names its census instruments and each resolves in the tree: `grep -rn 'stripped_strings' reckon/` returns three sites, all in `reckon/mcp_views.py` (2072 `authored_plan_text`, 2137 `_record_text_response`, 2238 `_section_response`); `grep -rnw '_TAG_RE' reckon/` returns the definition at `reckon/_plan_html.py:1804` and its single base use inside `count_open_decisions` at `:1823`; `_PROSE_SKIP_TAGS` sits at `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:148` as stated; the dispatch `get_text` reader is named; and `doccheck._prose_text` (`reckon/doccheck.py:298`) is a distinct element-scoped markdown linter, not a plan-section reader, so its omission from the census is correct rather than a gap.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §16 justifies `section_prose` as the merge of the three `stripped_strings` readers plus the dispatch `get_text` reader into one, and argues in its own text why the module-private coverage predicate is not a wrapper over `read_plan_review` (that reader joins one record to one digest; the predicate joins `roadmap.implementable_sections` to the union of section digests across `list_plan_reviews`).
